slides.title: Segment IoT without a *forklift*.
slides.body:
Thirty days.
The gear you already own.

slides.title: Days 1–10: profile what's talking
slides.body:
DHCP options and MAC OUI give you the vendor.
Flow data gives you *the truth*.

slides.title: Group by class, not vendor
slides.body:
Cameras. Badge readers. HVAC. Printers. Lab gear.
Class is what policy gets *written against*.

slides.title: Days 10–20: one VLAN per class
slides.body:
An ACL that permits everything and logs it.
You're *recording* the truth, not enforcing it.

slides.title: Pick the boring class first
slides.body: The camera vendor is not who you want as your *opening argument*.

slides.title: Days 20–30: the ACL writes itself
slides.body:
Cameras reach the NVR, NTP and DNS.
Nothing reaches the *user VLAN*.

slides.title: No new platform. No agent.
slides.body: Routed VLANs and access lists on hardware you *already pay maintenance on*.

slides.title: The hard part isn't technical.
slides.body:
Segmentation forces a conversation about who owns the cameras.
The network can enforce a policy. It can't invent one.

Follow *@mzsnetworks*
